title_ar: شرح نخبة الفكر في مصطلح أهل الأثر الشريط الأول
title_en: Commentary on Nukhbat al-Fikr on the terminology of the people of hadith — tape one
body_ar:
الشريط الأول

بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم

الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين السلام عليكم ورحمة الله وبركاته.

أما بعد فإن طلب العلم من أهم ما يتقرب به إلى الله سبحانه وتعالى، فهو جهاد في سبيل الله وقد أخرج مالك في الموطإ عن أبي بكر بن عبد الرحمن من خرج إلى المسجد لا يخرجه إلا علم يعلمه أو يتعلمه كان كالمجاهد في سبيل الله رجع غانما، وصح عن النبي الحض على تعلم سنته، وقد أمر الله سبحانه وتعالى بتعليمها للناس فقال تعالى في خطابه لأمهات المؤمنين: {واذكرن ما يتلى في بيوتكن من آيات الله والحكمة}..
body_en:
Tape one.

In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate.

Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement. Peace be upon you, and the mercy of God and His blessings.

To proceed: the seeking of knowledge is among the most important means by which one draws near to God, glorified and exalted; it is a struggle in the path of God. Malik recorded in the Muwaṭṭaʾ, from Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman: whoever goes out to the mosque, nothing taking him out but knowledge that he teaches or learns, is like one who struggles in the path of God and has returned with spoils. It is soundly established from the Prophet that he urged the learning of his sunnah, and God, glorified and exalted, has commanded that it be taught to the people, for God Most High said, addressing the Mothers of the Believers: {And remember what is recited in your houses of the signs of God and of the wisdom} (Sūrat al-Aḥzāb 33:34)..

flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT, minor. The download-link label on this record is misspelt with a doubled mīm; every other record in this range spells it correctly. It is a navigation element rather than part of the text, so it has been removed from body_ar along with the correctly spelt labels elsewhere and is recorded only here. Noted because it shows the labels were typed by hand per record rather than generated, which bears on how reliable other per-record boilerplate in this corpus is.

translator_notes: Qur'anic and hadith renderings in this file are interpretive translations of meaning, offered to carry the Sheikh's argument in English. They are not a substitute for the Arabic.
The date shown by the CMS is a bulk-upload timestamp shared by every item in this range, not the date the Sheikh gave the answer. The real date of composition is unknown. See date_is_cms_bulk_upload.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on Ibn Hajar al-ʿAsqalani's Nukhbat al-Fikr, a short manual of hadith terminology. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 628–637 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and even then a gap remains (see the note on the download filenames).

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text is the opening of a lecture and breaks off; the full transcript is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.

The report from the Muwaṭṭaʾ is given without the quotation marks the source uses for other reports, and it is a statement of Abu Bakr ibn ʿAbd al-Rahman, a Successor, rather than a saying traced to the Prophet. The Sheikh attributes it to Malik in the Muwaṭṭaʾ and gives no grading; none has been supplied.

'It is soundly established from the Prophet' renders ṣaḥḥa ʿan al-nabī. The source omits the honorific after 'the Prophet' at this one point, where it supplies it everywhere else; the omission is in the source and body_ar preserves it.
'The Mothers of the Believers' are the wives of the Prophet, whom the verse addresses.
The verse reference has been supplied per house style; the source gives the verse text alone.
